subject: Order Form: renewal cadence & notice stacking (Greylight)
messages:
From: Alice Barnes <alice.barnes@greylighthealth.com>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.ai>
Cc: Greylight Health Procurement <procurement@greylighthealth.com>
Date: Mon, 29 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Order Form: renewal cadence & notice stacking

Hi Mateo —

Thanks for sending the draft Order Form last week. Our legal and procurement teams are reviewing and surfaced two items we need to clarify before internal approval:

1) Auto-renew mechanics: the draft has a 1-year term with automatic renewal for successive 12-month terms unless either party gives notice 60 days before renewal. Procurement wants either a shorter notice window (45 days) or a defined renewal-notice staggering for pilots converting to committed seats.

2) Termination for convenience (TFC): the MSA allows TFC but the playbook references a 60-day offboarding SLA tied to dedicated capacity. We need clarity on whether TFC applies to the pilot-period pricing and whether there are pro-rated refunds or obligations for reserved capacity.

Can your team confirm whether Redwood can:
- Support a 45-day renewal notice for pilot accounts converting within 6 months, or alternatively allow a one-time 30- to 45-day carveout?
- Provide a short summary of options for TFC financial treatment (pro rata refund, committed-usage true-up, or transition credits)?

We attached our internal suggested edits to the Order Form (Greylight_Draft_OrderForm_v2.docx). Appreciate a quick turnaround — procurement has an internal deadline of 4/6.

Best,
Alice
Alice Barnes
Director, Strategic Procurement
Greylight Health

---
Attachment: Greylight_Draft_OrderForm_v2.docx (docx, 142KB)

From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.ai>
To: Alice Barnes <alice.barnes@greylighthealth.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 29 Mar 2027 11:09:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Order Form: renewal cadence & notice stacking

Hi Alice —

Thanks — looping in our contracts and commercial ops folks to confirm options (cc'd). High-level answers below so you can pass to procurement while we pull redlines: 

- Renewal notice: we can accommodate a 45-day notice for customers converting from a pilot to committed capacity if the conversion is requested within 6 months of pilot start. That will require us to add a one-time election clause in the Order Form so we don't leave dedicated capacity exposed.

- TFC financial treatment: options we typically offer are (a) pro rata refund of prepaid usage for hosted/consumption invoices, (b) true-up for reserved/dedicated capacity (shortfall billed through end of the then-current monthly billing period or negotiated transition credits), or (c) a blended transition credit on a case-by-case basis for early buyer commitments.

I'll ask Laura to draft the language for a one-time pilot-conversion renewal notice carveout and Ben to prepare a clean TFC schedule with the three financial treatment options for your procurement team to pick from. Expect a redline back by tomorrow EOD.

—Mateo
Mateo Alvarez
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
mateo.alvarez@redwood.ai | +1-415-555-0172

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Alice Barnes <alice.barnes@greylighthealth.com>, Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 29 Mar 2027 16:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Order Form: renewal cadence & notice stacking

Hi Alice —

Attaching a proposed redline for the Order Form and a companion TFC schedule (see attachment). Key points in the redline: 

• Pilot conversion carveout (Section 2.1): one-time election by Customer to convert pilot to committed term within 6 months of pilot start; if elected, renewal notice window is 45 days for the first renewal only.

• Termination for Convenience (TFC) schedule (Addendum A):
  - Hosted/consumption: pro rata refund for unused prepaid amounts, processed within 30 days of termination.
  - Dedicated/reserved: 30-day billing true-up plus option for a negotiated transition credit equal to up to 25% of remaining committed fees if Customer returns capacity within 90 days to mitigate stranded hardware.
  - Pilot-specific pricing: if TFC exercised during pilot, standard cancellation fee waived if conversion election not made, but Customer remains responsible for consumed usage through termination date.

We tried to balance procurement's need for flexibility with our capacity risk. Karthik, can you review the wording and flag any legal concerns before we send to Alice?

Thanks,
Laura
Laura Bennett
Senior Commercial Counsel, Redwood Inference

---
Attachment: Redwood_Termination_Playbook.pdf (pdf, 78KB)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 30 Mar 2027 09:37:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Order Form: renewal cadence & notice stacking

Laura / team —

Thanks for the quick draft. A couple of legal redline notes: 

1) The one-time pilot-conversion carveout is acceptable but we should add a firm mechanism to record election (DocuSign checkbox or an election field in the Order Form) to avoid later disputes about whether the carveout was invoked.

2) For Dedicated/reserved true-up: the proposed "30-day billing true-up" needs to be clarified to say the Customer pays for the proportion of reserved capacity for the remainder of the current billing period (not necessarily 30 days) or we use a pro-rated calculation tied to the committed term. Suggested language: "Customer shall be liable for fees accrued through the end of the then-current billing cycle, calculated on a pro rata basis."

3) Transition credit: legal is comfortable with the concept but recommends removing the numeric cap (25%) from the contract and instead leaving credit amounts negotiable and documented in the Order Form to preserve flexibility across deals.

I've made line edits in the attached redline. Once we get procurement feedback we should capture the final election and any negotiated credit in an addendum to the Order Form so billing and finance have a clear record.

-Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Head of Legal — Commercial Contracts, Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.ai

Thanks Laura / Karthik — this is helpful. Procurement reviewed the redline and the team is generally comfortable with the approach. A few follow-ups before we finalize: 

• Election capture: procurement would prefer the DocuSign checkbox to be explicit language in the Order Form (not just the attachable addendum) — they asked for the exact election text so their signature block captures intent.

• Transition credit: Greylight would like a baseline formula we can reference (e.g., "up to 25% of remaining committed fees, subject to mutually agreed conditions") rather than leaving it entirely open — that helps our internal approvers understand worst-case liability. If Redwood insists on negotiable amounts, can you add an example calculation in the addendum?

• Timing: given our April 6 internal deadline, can we aim to have a final Order Form (with election text filled and an example transition-credit calc) by EOD Thursday 4/1?

If you can hit that timeline we'll route for final signatures on Friday. Thanks for the quick turnaround.

Best,
Alice

Director, Strategic Procurement
Greylight Health
